title: New French Literary Prize Rewards Books Written with AI
paragraphs: A new literary prize in France will reward books written with the help of artificial intelligence.
The Prix Pascal de Littérature IA was started by three French technology entrepreneurs — Philippe Rodriguez, Albin Serviant and Gilles Mentré — and is open to anyone who writes in French.
To enter, writers must submit an unpublished work of fiction of between 10,000 and 50,000 words co-written with AI. They can use any of the major AI tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and more.

However, applicants have to be open about how they used the technology. Along with their manuscript, they must submit the name of the AI model used, as well as the prompts and methods they used to create the story.
The organizers say the submitted works should in some way pertain to an ethical, social or ecological problem threatening humanity.

Applications opened on October 20, and will close at the end of November. A jury of writers, critics, publishers, philosophers and journalists will choose 10 finalists before selecting a winner in early December. The winning work will be published.
The prize comes as other literary competitions grapple with how to deal with AI.

In September, Canadian-Haitian writer Thélyson Orélien was removed from the longlist for France's most prestigious literary prize, the Prix Goncourt, amid allegations that he had used AI to write his novel, It Was Either That or Die. The critically acclaimed book had already sold about 35,000 copies.
Orélien denied the claims, but his Canadian publisher later said it had confirmed that AI had been used in the writing process, and ended its relationship with him.
Other major writing prizes, including the Caine Prize for African writers and the Commonwealth Short Story Prize, have also faced allegations that winning entries were created with AI.
And in Japan, a 20-year-old short poetry competition ended in February after organizers said it had become too difficult to tell whether some entries had been written by humans or AI.
